title: Why NBC is betting big on Lincoln Riley orchestrating a USC turnaround
text: Why NBC is betting big on Lincoln Riley orchestrating a USC turnaround NBC has shown its share of USC football games in prime time this season, but will Lincoln Riley and USC make it 'must-see' college football TV? USC coach Lincoln Riley, center, leads his team onto the field before a win over San José State in August. NBC has featured USC six times in nine games, making the Trojans its West Coast anchor as the network tries to compete with ABC’s dominant prime-time college football audience. The network is betting Lincoln Riley can revive national interest in USC, with Saturday’s game against No. 2 Ohio State at the Coliseum offering the Trojans a prime-time chance to play spoiler.week’s matchup with No. 2 Ohio State marks the sixth time in nine games that USC will be featured on NBC. That’s already tied for the most any one network has aired a Big Ten team since 2024, when the conference expanded to 18 teams.‘I’m the right person to be here. ’ Embattled Lincoln Riley stresses his bond with USC Amid rising tensions as Lincoln Riley has fallen short of leading USC to the College Football Playoff, he insists he is the right fit for the Trojans,. But going all-in on the Cardinal and Gold wasn’t necessarily the network’s plan going into the season, according to Justin Byczek, NBC’s executive vice president of programming and rights management. It just worked out that way.“It’s effectively a draft, and we’re trying to look at different weeks and prioritize,” Byczek said. “One of the first things that jumped out at us was how important thatWhen the three networks divided up the Big Ten’s TV games last spring, Byczek said NBC also zeroed in on that game, as well as USC’s matchups with Ohio State andJust by virtue of its geography and its brand, USC makes for a natural fit in NBC’s prime-time slot , similar to how FOX’s Big Noon Saturday regularly features Ohio State in its early window.Those prime-time matchups featuring the Trojans, though, have lagged a bit behind other top teams from the Big Ten and SEC. USC’s matchup with Oregon drew the largest audience of its season to date, with 5 million viewers on NBC and Peacock. That’s the only time this season that a USC game has finished in the top five of the week’s most viewed games, according to Nielsen data.No. 16 USC sees its playoff hopes take a serious hit in a 24-7 loss to Wisconsin following what was arguably the Trojans’ worst performance of the season on offense. That’s a conference-wide issue. The Big Ten has only had the week’s most-watched game twice this season, once on CBS and another time on Fox .Otherwise, ABC has dominated, with more than 10 million tuning in most weeks to the network’s prime-time game. So, in order to compete with ABC in prime time, NBC is betting on Lincoln Riley and the Trojans as its West Coast anchor.“Because they’re intriguing — not only in Los Angeles, but nationally,” Eagle said. “College football fans want to see if they can get over the hump. Can Lincoln Riley get them there? ” That question will no doubt come up on the broadcast this week.And with three Big Ten games still left after that, you can bet it won’t be the last time we hear it asked on NBC. Ryan Kartje is the USC beat writer at the Los Angeles Times. He joined The Times after six years with the Southern California News Group. A Michigan native and University of Michigan graduate, Kartje previously wrote for Fox Sports Wisconsin and the Bloomington Herald-Times.
summary: NBC has featured USC six times in nine games, making the Trojans its West Coast anchor as the network tries to compete with ABC’s dominant prime-time college football audience. But going all-in on the Cardinal and Gold wasn’t necessarily the network’s plan going into the season, according to Justin Byczek, NBC’s executive vice president of programming and rights management.
